title: 2026 UK CBAM record-retention and penalty QA controls

sources.title: Keeping records for Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
Prepare for the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)

facts.source_fact: CBAM records may be kept in written form including electronic records.
The general retention period is six years from the later of creation date or end of the relevant accounting period.
HMRC states a fixed £500 penalty may be charged for failure to keep CBAM records.
Separate penalties may apply for failure to provide information or documents requested by HMRC.
facts.expected_handling: Keep recordkeeping and information-request penalties separate.

facts.source_fact: Recordkeeping applies even where an importer does not ultimately need to register if evidence is needed to show non-liability.
facts.expected_handling: Do not equate registration with all record duties.

facts.source_fact: Retention rules support later return, relief, repayment and exemption evidence.
A potential penalty does not prove that HMRC has assessed a penalty in a particular case.
Record retention is an importer compliance requirement, not emissions measurement.
The guidance was first published on 16 July 2026.
